title: Working Hours and Attendance
content: Standard working hours are 9 hours per day including a 1-hour break. Core hours, when everyone should be available, are 11:00 to 16:00. Three late arrivals of more than 30 minutes in a month count as one half-day casual leave deduction.

title: Work From Home Policy
content: Employees may work from home up to 2 days per week with manager approval. WFH days must be marked in the attendance system in advance. Interns and employees on probation are not eligible for regular WFH.

title: Casual Leave Entitlement
content: Every full-time employee gets 12 casual leave days per calendar year. Casual leave can be taken in half-day units. Unused casual leave does not carry over to the next year.

title: Sick Leave
content: Employees get 8 paid sick leave days per year. A medical certificate is required if sick leave exceeds 2 consecutive days. Unused sick leave does not carry over.

title: Earned (Privilege) Leave
content: Employees earn 1.5 days of earned leave per month of service (18 days per year). Up to 30 days can be carried forward to the next year. Earned leave above 30 days lapses, and it can be encashed only at the time of exit.

title: Maternity Leave
content: Female employees are entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two children and 12 weeks from the third child onward. Leave can begin up to 8 weeks before the expected delivery date. Employees should inform HR at least 30 days before the planned start date.

title: Paternity Leave
content: Male employees are entitled to 10 working days of paid paternity leave. It must be taken within 3 months of the child's birth and can be split into at most two blocks.

title: Bereavement Leave
content: Employees get 5 paid days of bereavement leave on the death of an immediate family member (spouse, child, parent, sibling). For other relatives, up to 2 days can be taken from casual leave.

title: Compensatory Off (Comp-Off)
content: An employee who works on a weekend or company holiday at the manager's request earns one comp-off day. Comp-off must be requested within 30 days of the worked day and approved by the manager. Expired comp-off is not paid out.

title: Leave Without Pay (LWP)
content: When all paid leave is used up, employees may apply for leave without pay. LWP requires prior manager and HR approval. LWP over 15 days in one stretch needs HR head approval. Salary is deducted pro-rata for LWP days.

title: Company Holidays
content: The company observes 12 paid holidays per year. The official holiday list is published every December on the intranet. Employees may swap up to 2 fixed holidays for optional holidays of their choice.

title: Salary Payment and Payslips
content: Salary is credited on the last working day of each month. Payslips are available on the HR portal by the 3rd of the next month. Payroll queries must be raised within 30 days of the salary credit.

title: Tax Declarations and Form 16
content: Employees submit tax-saving investment declarations in April and proofs in January. Form 16 is issued by 15 June each year. Missing proofs result in higher TDS in the last quarter of the financial year.

title: Group Health Insurance
content: All full-time employees are covered under the group health insurance policy with a sum insured of 5 lakh rupees, effective from the date of joining. Spouse, children, and parents can be added as dependents during enrollment. Cashless treatment is available at network hospitals.

title: Provident Fund (PF)
content: Both employee and employer contribute 12 percent of basic salary to the provident fund. The UAN is shared by HR within 2 weeks of joining. PF withdrawal is handled directly on the EPFO portal after exit.

title: Learning and Certification Reimbursement
content: Employees can claim up to 30,000 rupees per year for job-relevant courses and certifications. Manager approval is needed before enrolling. Claims need the payment receipt and the completion certificate. Employees who leave within 12 months of a reimbursed course may have to repay the amount.

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement
content: Business travel must be approved by the manager before booking. Expense claims need original bills and must be submitted within 30 days of the trip. Reimbursement is processed with the next salary cycle after approval.

title: Code of Conduct and POSH
content: The company has a zero-tolerance policy on harassment and discrimination. Complaints under the POSH policy go to the Internal Committee and are handled confidentially. Employees should not discuss ongoing complaints with colleagues.

title: Performance Appraisal Cycle
content: Appraisals happen once a year in April for the previous financial year. Employees who joined after 1 October are reviewed in the next cycle. Probation lasts 6 months, after which the employee becomes permanent through a written letter from HR.

title: Resignation Notice Period
content: The standard notice period is 30 days for employees on probation and 60 days for permanent employees. Notice must be submitted in writing to the manager and HR. Early release or notice buyout is not automatic and needs approval from the HR head.

title: Full and Final Settlement
content: Full and final settlement is processed within 45 days of the last working day, after all company assets are returned and clearance is complete. The relieving and experience letters are issued after settlement is done.
